newsitem.title: UK: Sedgwick lifts H1 despite strong pound.
newsitem.headline: Sedgwick lifts H1 despite strong pound.

text.p: An improved performance in the United States helped British insurance broker Sedgwick Group increase first half profits on Tuesday despite continuing weak insurance rates and the adverse impact of the pound.
Pre-tax profits rose to 66.5 million pounds over the six months from 64.1 million pounds a year earlier.
Excluding the effect of the currency which took seven million pounds off headline numbers, profits were up 16 percent over the period.
For the year as a whole the group expects the pound to take just under 9 million pounds off profits.
Shares gave a muted response to the figures which were broadly in-line with analyst forecasts, adding one pence to 120 pence.
Chairman Sax Riley described the performance as encouraging and said the group's strategy of expanding the range of services offered to clients through its worldwide network was continuing.
And he once again hinted that Sedgwick would not rule out the possibility of a merger with British rival Willis Corroon.
Sedgwick had made it clear that it wanted to grow in size and increase turnover, said Riley.
"You have to compare what we have said and what (Willis chairman) John Reeve has said and draw your own conclusions," he said.
Some analysts suggest a tie-up with Willis could provide the two companies with a solution to the problems posed by the intense competition and slim margins.
They argue something dramatic is needed to close the gap with U.S. rivals Aon and Marsh & Mclennan.
Sedgwick said it aimed to continue with small, add on purchases particularly in continental Europe as long as they provided shareholder value and gave Sedgwick management and dividend policy control.
Earlier this month it confirmed a 50 million pound joint venture with Italy's leading broker Nikols Brichetto.
Nikols will own 51 percent of the merged operations but crucially Sedgwick will have a majority of voting rights.
Riley repeated his view that the shares remain undervalued with U.S. brokers commanding ratings of as much as 40 percent higher.
Sedgwick's operational strategy has been geared at lessening the group's dependence on the underwriting cycle by increasing fee-earning consultancy business.
The aim is to move to a 50/50 split of fee to brokerage from the current 37/67 division.

Sedgwick has also concentrated on broadening its business base and keeping a tight control of costs and it said it was well advanced on a number of initiatives intended to significantly improve operational effectiveness and reduce costs.
The employees benefits operation, Sedgwick Noble Lowndes, continued to report increased profits and that trend is expected to continue for the rest of the year.

The results included 7.4 million pounds from Sedgwick Oakwood Lloyd's Underwriting Agents. Last year these were included in the third quarter because of uncertainty relating to Lloyd's reconstruction and Renewal plan (R&R).
Riley said the Sedgwick was totally committed to completing its pension misselling review and was satisfied it had adequate provisions to cover the costs.
In June, Treasury minister Helen Liddell singled out Sedgwick over its response to the government's call for action over misselling.
But Riley stressed the company was keen to put the matter behind it and had 100 staff working round the clock to reach its target.
